messages.subject: Rstan manual multivariate hierarchical regression example: row_vector problem in multi_normal
parts:
Hi all

I am trying to recreate the multivariate regression example from page 92 (section 9.9) in the most recent Rstan manual, as it fits the type of analysis that I want to run on a psychological experiment.

My goal is to adjust the subject level data (‘groups’) that I have with the population/group-level predictors. Each subject undertakes 22 trials in a decision-making task, with binary responses. Hence I am using a linear regression model at the group level and a logistic function at the subject level.

My problem is that I am running into a well-documented problem: I am creating a row-vector in line 27 when multiplying the group predictors (u[s]) with gamma. the multi-normal function only accepts vectors as inputs:

Error in stanc("GBE_hierarchical_logistic_linear.stan") : 

  failed to parse Stan model 'GBE_hierarchical_logistic_linear' with error message:

EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=input; line=27, column=56

    beta[s] ~ multi_normal((u[s] * gamma), Sigma_beta);

                                                       ^-- here

DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:

no matches for function name="multi_normal_log"

    arg 0 type=vector

    arg 1 type=row vector

    arg 2 type=matrix

available function signatures for multi_normal_log:

0.  multi_normal_log(vector, vector, matrix) : real

unknown distribution=multi_normal

Parser expecting: <eps>


I simulated data to test this model. The simulated data is structured as follows: 50 subjects, three parameters to be estimated per subject, two group predictors, each subject's true parameters are drawn from a normal distribution, with non-zero mean and std. of 3.  

My questions:

1. Since I have exactly recreated the example rstan code given on page 95; I wonder whether I made a mistake or whether the example as described in the manual cannot currently be run in rstan given the row_vector restriction in the multi_normal function.

2. As my data has to be structured the way it is set up, I wonder whether there is a work around for me? I saw that the issue (#589) is fixed on the development platform.

Please find attached my stan code; a matlab file that simulates data; the matlab data output (mat file); the code that runs the rstan model. Note that R.matlab has to be installed to read the mat file into R.

For some reason the file upload isn't working, here's a dropbox link: https://www.dropbox.com/sh/hx7gqkcy3b3sjah/AACIyOcjzXmNY76Xx89d0mf4a

Thank you very much for your help in advance!

Daniel

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Rstan manual multivariate hierarchical regression example: row_vector problem in multi_normal
parts:
Thanks for looking for answers and sorry the list is so hard
to search!

For now, the simplest thing to do is transpose (postfix ' operator),
so you'd use:
beta[s]' ~ multi_normal((u[s] * gamma), Sigma_beta);

A more efficient alternative would to be declare beta as
an array of vectors (I'm not actually sure what M and N
should be in your case --- this assumes beta was declared as
an M x N matrix).

vector[N] beta[M];

There's a discussion of vectors/matrices vs. arrays and efficiency
in a chapter of the manual.

The generalization and vectorization of multi_normal hasn't
been merged into develop yet, but it's going to be soon and
will be in the next release, 2.3.0, which we hope to get out later
this week or early next week.

Here's the issue and pull request to track:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/589

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/pull/608

When Marco's fix is merged, your original code will work as written.

- Bob

On Wed, Jun 25, 2014 at 4:36 PM, Daniel Grigat <daniel...@icloud.com> wrote:
Hi Bob

Sorry that I have to bother you with this again. I just updated to the new rstan version, however the error persists (see in red at the end of this post).
The issue is with how you're calling multi_normal_log() and updating to a new rstan version isn't going to help.

I tried to transpose, as you suggested but that doesnt work either. I am not sure whether transforming beta (either by transposing or changing beta to an array of vectors) would change anything, as rstan seems to complain about the (u[s] * gamma) operation.

You need to transpose the (u[s] * gamma) operation. The error message is telling you that the the second argument, (u[s] * gamma), is a row_vector. The available function signatures expects that to be a vector. In Stan, vector and row_vector are not equivalent.
Has the multi_normal issue not been fixed? What should I do?
Is there an issue we're not aware of? The fix is to use the types correctly. That is, make sure the second argument is actually a vector, not a row vector. Can you try transposing the expression?

Thanks
